messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: high router p95 latency spike (threshold=200ms) in us-west-2 canary. Triggered 1 times. Incident ID: pd_99321
elaine: seeing it on the dashboard too, canaries up ~220-300ms for a couple mins
raj: acked — taking it. Oncall-1 for the shift.
morgan: +1 acked, will follow if it persists. any customer reports?
elaine: no 1:1 customer noise on slack or support. synthetic canary only so far.
incident-bot: Auto-resolve rule: if metric returns under threshold for 3m, auto-resolve will run. Current state: firing.
raj: quick check of router pods, run: ```kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=router -o wide``` shows one pod restarting once in last 5m, others fine.
elaine: logs on that pod look like transient connection reset to model-worker, kv-cache warmups around same time. snippet: ```2026-03-15T10:01:23Z ERR connection reset by peer```
morgan: likely transient worker GC/oom? mem graphs show a tiny bump but below limit. scaling seemed fine.
raj: I'll hold for 3m window. If it drops, let PD auto-resolve, otherwise we'll silence and roll back the last canary config change.
elaine: agree. also setting a narrow silence for this rule to avoid churn: `pd silence pd_99321 for 15m if canary only` (doing it now)
incident-bot: Silence created by elaine: pd_99321 — duration 15m — scope: canary/us-west-2.
morgan: nice, that should stop noisy repeats. keeping an eye on aggregate latency.
raj: latency trending down, p95 back to ~95ms. good. waiting 1m to confirm.
elaine: auto-resolve triggered: PagerDuty alert pd_99321 auto-resolved at 3276543355.
raj: good sign. quick post-check: no customer-facing errors in logs, traffic unaffected, no rollback necessary. marking as transient/no-impact. :thumbsup:
sre-rotations: leaving note on the runbook: "pd_99321 — transient router thrum; actions taken: ack, narrow silence, observed KV warmup, monitor 10m, no rollback"
morgan: handing back to normal ops. closing thread unless it flaps again.
elaine: thanks team. filing a short blameless note in incidents with timeline.
